
UPDATE-WORK-UNIT
Update work unit metadata including title, description, epic association, and parent relationship

WHEN TO USE
  Use this command to modify work unit metadata after creation. Common use cases: refining title/description, changing epic association, or restructuring parent-child relationships. NOTE: Work unit type (story/bug/task) is immutable and cannot be changed.

PREREQUISITES
  • Work unit must exist in spec/work-units.json

USAGE
  fspec update-work-unit <workUnitId> [options]

ARGUMENTS
  <workUnitId> (required)
    Work unit ID to update (e.g., AUTH-001)

OPTIONS
  -t, --title <title>
    New title for the work unit
  -d, --description <description>
    New description for the work unit
  -e, --epic <epic>
    Epic ID to associate with (moves work unit to new epic)
  -p, --parent <parent>
    Parent work unit ID (for hierarchical relationships, prevents circular references)

COMMON PATTERNS
  • Refine work unit details
    Example: # Initial creation
fspec create-story AUTH "User auth"

# Refine after Example Mapping
fspec update-work-unit AUTH-001 --title "OAuth 2.0 authentication" --description "Implement OAuth 2.0 flow with Google"
    undefined

  • Reorganize epic structure
    Example: # Move work units to different epic
fspec update-work-unit AUTH-001 --epic SECURITY
fspec update-work-unit AUTH-002 --epic SECURITY

# Verify epic structure
fspec show-epic SECURITY
    undefined

  • Create parent-child relationships
    Example: # Break large work unit into subtasks
fspec create-story AUTH "OAuth implementation" --parent AUTH-001
fspec create-task AUTH "OAuth testing" --parent AUTH-001

# View hierarchy
fspec show-work-unit AUTH-001
    undefined


TYPICAL WORKFLOW
  1. View current metadata: fspec show-work-unit <workUnitId> → 2. Update fields: fspec update-work-unit <workUnitId> --title "New title" → 3. Verify changes: fspec show-work-unit <workUnitId>

EXAMPLES
  1. Update work unit title
  $ fspec update-work-unit AUTH-001 --title "OAuth 2.0 integration"
  ✓ Work unit AUTH-001 updated successfully

  2. Update work unit description
  $ fspec update-work-unit AUTH-001 --description "Implement OAuth 2.0 authentication flow"
  ✓ Work unit AUTH-001 updated successfully

  3. Move work unit to different epic
  $ fspec update-work-unit AUTH-001 --epic AUTH
  ✓ Work unit AUTH-001 updated successfully

  4. Set parent-child relationship
  $ fspec update-work-unit AUTH-002 --parent AUTH-001
  ✓ Work unit AUTH-002 updated successfully

  5. Update multiple fields at once
  $ fspec update-work-unit AUTH-001 --title "New title" --description "New description" --epic API
  ✓ Work unit AUTH-001 updated successfully

COMMON ERRORS
  ✗ Work unit 'AUTH-999' does not exist
    Fix: Verify the work unit ID exists with: fspec list-work-units

  ✗ Epic 'NONEXISTENT' does not exist
    Fix: Check available epics with: fspec list-epics or create epic with: fspec create-epic

  ✗ Parent work unit 'AUTH-999' does not exist
    Fix: Verify parent ID exists with: fspec list-work-units

  ✗ Circular parent relationship detected
    Fix: Cannot set parent to a work unit that is already a descendant. Check hierarchy with: fspec show-work-unit <id>

  ✗ Work unit type is immutable and cannot be changed after creation
    Fix: Delete this work unit and create a new one with the correct type (story/bug/task)

RELATED COMMANDS
  fspec show-work-unit
  fspec update-work-unit-status
  fspec update-work-unit-estimate
  fspec create-story
  fspec create-bug
  fspec create-task
  fspec list-work-units

NOTES
  • Provide at least one option (--title, --description, --epic, or --parent)
  • Work unit type is immutable - delete and recreate to change type
  • Changing epic moves work unit from old epic to new epic automatically
  • Parent-child relationships are validated for circular references
  • Epic references are automatically updated in spec/epics.json
  • Parent references update children arrays in both old and new parent work units
  • UpdatedAt timestamp is automatically set to current time
